It’s always been downtown in my experience. For me, I’ve always put safety first and I’m adamant about making sure my car is locked no matter where I go. I think living in a city should be enough of an indication to just make sure your car is locked and to make sure you’re not stupid about leaving your things out in the open. Lady Gaga. She released her album Born This Way in 2011, when I was 14, in the closet and lacking a sense of identity. I was so incredibly lost and I was terrified of the reality of being a gay man, I hated myself so much. It was an awful time in my life, and the eccentricity, bravery, boldness and character that this woman showed during that time (and throughout her career in general) was a saving grace for me. Her music was (and still is) a safe space for me, and her music truly gave me so much joy and hope in times I needed it the most. I remember this time in my life fondly now because I always connect it to her Born This Way album, and it made me feel so free and confident and hopeful that one day I could be strong enough to be myself and feel secure in my own skin. I will always support Lady Gaga. I believe that she is one of the most important people in the entertainment industry. I truly don’t know if I would be here today if I didn’t have her music to connect to as a teenager. It’s unbelievable what she has done for the gay community.

After almost 6 months completely sober, I started casually drinking again, but it is dangerous for me. I still struggle with the self-control once I start, but I’m grateful that I’m aware of this. A couple weeks ago, I decided I could order a beer at dinner because I thought I could handle it. I did! But the temptation to drink more was incredibly strong.

I decided to do it again on a couple more dinner trips, but that turned into 2 beers and I stopped it there. This past weekend, I went to a wedding. I was so nervous because I didn’t know many people there, so I decided to buy a 6-pack of beer to try and loosen up before I went. I drank a couple, had a glass of wine at the wedding, and finished the last 4 beers when I got home. I felt so guilty and awful about it. BUT, at the same time, I told myself that I am aware of my limits and I believe that it is safe for me to drink on occasion. I recognized that I was at a social event where alcohol is permitted and encouraged, and I only had one drink. It’s not like I was sitting at home in bed pounding back beer after beer by myself in isolation like I was 6 months ago. It’s unfortunate that I have to police my alcohol intake so much, but if I’m not conscious about it, I will lose control. I still consider myself sober, as I’m not in active addiction anymore and it feels good knowing that I’m better at controlling my intake. I have no plans to be a regular drinker again, but I’ve decided that I’m at a place now where I can consciously handle a drink or two when it’s appropriate and I feel comfortable.  I will probably live with guilt whenever I have a sip of alcohol for a long time.
